answer: At most 5 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a jetty tag. The sable cap is upheld at intake and saffron shows the per-origin counts. A datacenter or proxy pool therefore cannot mint a army of identities in one epoch no matter how much capital it holds, since each account consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. That is 9 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
